text:
elena: Quick heads-up — canary for AWQ dynamic-group sizing revealed intermittent token drops on long prompts after we tightened act-quant bucketing. Pasting quick notes and logs.

sam: ok, what exactly failed? repro reliably?

elena: Not 100% deterministic but reproducible on our long-dialog suite (>1024 tokens) with bursty batch mixes. Key numbers: baseline FP32 throughput ~1200 req/s, AWQ (group_size=auto, act_buckets=8) throughput ~1050 req/s but p95 latency spikes to ~280ms. Accuracy (LLM-eval set) delta for act_buckets=8: -0.8% vs FP32; act_buckets=16: -0.2%. The token-drop is orthogonal to bulk accuracy loss — it manifests as missing tokens / early termination on ~3-5% of long examples.

mike: logs?

elena: snippet from runtime: 
```
[2024-11-02T14:02:11Z] WARN awq/runtime: kv_cache_boundary_mismatch detected, group_id=17, expected_len=512, got_len=496
[2024-11-02T14:02:11Z] ERROR awq/decode: emitted_eos_early, prompt_id=Qv8, tokens_emitted=987
[2024-11-02T14:02:11Z] DEBUG awq/actq: buckets=8, mean_bucket_width=0.128, max_residual=0.34
```

elena: hypothesis: coarse act quant buckets produce sharp activation quantization at group boundaries; when dynamic grouping changes group boundary mid-request (due to batching/kv cache reuse), fused kernel sees mismatched kv sizes and drops tokens.

kai: sounds plausible. quick test: fix group_size to a small constant and increase act_buckets. Did you try fixed configs?

elena: yes — quick canary with group_size=32 + act_buckets=16 removed the token-skip in our suite. Metrics: p95 down to ~180ms, throughput -6% (from 1050 -> 990 req/s), accuracy delta improved to -0.15% vs FP32.

anika: tl;dr: safer to prioritize correctness for now. We should avoid auto dynamic split on long requests until we have per-batch compatibility checks.

elena: proposed immediate mitigations: 
- pin group_size per-model to 32 for this canary vs auto
- increase act_buckets to 16 by default for llama-2-13b awq builds
- add runtime assert to detect kv_cache_mismatch and trigger transparent fallback to FP8 variant or serialized single-request execution
- add targeted eval prompts (long-dialogs) to CI to catch regressions

mike: can add eval tests. sample config I used to repro: 
```yaml
model: llama-2-13b
quant: awq
act_buckets: 8
group_size: auto
kv_prealloc: true
dynamic_group_policy:
  latency_target_ms: 200
  min_group: 16
  max_group: 96
```

elena: and the safe config that fixed it: 
```yaml
model: llama-2-13b
quant: awq
act_buckets: 16
group_size: 32
kv_prealloc: true
dynamic_group_policy: disabled
```

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for model=llama-2-13b@awq-fixed-32-16, canary_size=5% :rocket:

sam: rollout plan suggestion — gradual 5/20/50 with 10m watch windows, realtime token-drop monitor that cancels rollout if >1% token-drop or if p95 regresses >20%. Also add automatic fallback to fp8-quant variant when kv mismatch seen.

elena: agreed. I'll add runtime guard + monitor. Will open a short RFC for per-model safe-mode and add the long-dialog eval set to monthly regressions.

ops-bot: ticket created: TICKET-8421 - "awq kv_cache boundary mismatch / failover" (priority=P1)

mike: I'll bake the long-dialog suite into the nightly eval harness and add a small stress test that randomizes batch mixes to exercise dynamic grouping.

elena: thanks all — I'll update the canary docs and tag infra to reserve fallback capacity. Filing follow-ups: RFC + test plan + auto-fallback implementation notes. :thumbsup:
